data.narrative:
Anthrogen is a Seed-stage biotech company founded by Ankit Singhal, Connor Lee, and Vignesh Karthik, having raised $4M to date. The valuation landscape includes 3 public comparables in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers, though no narrow peer set of same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with sufficient data density exists for direct median benchmarking.

Given data constraints, only the Stage-Progression method is reliably applicable. Using total capital raised ($4M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier yields an implied valuation of $10M. The Public-Comp Anchoring approach cannot be deployed because Anthrogen's revenue is not disclosed—a typical constraint for early-stage private companies. The Peer-Median method similarly fails: while 7 same-sector peers exist in the broader Biotech & Health universe, none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or comparable tier), and relying on all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $8M to $12M, centered on $10M. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based valuation anchors, lack of tightly comparable Seed-stage peers, and limited visibility into Anthrogen's technical progress or clinical milestones. Any refinement would require either disclosed revenue figures or a deeper private peer dataset stratified by stage.
